title: Deep centers had a larger late share of nearby M5.5+ counts than shallow centers at 200 km in ComCat, 2001-2024
abstract: We tested the share of nearby post-event counts on days 7 to 30 among counts on days 1 to 30. We used a fixed USGS ComCat snapshot, 646 shallow and 99 deep M6.5 to below 8 centers in 2001-2024, symmetric isolation and a 200 km depth-aware chord. After magnitude-bin adjustment, the late share was 46.18% for shallow and 67.47% for deep centers. The deep-minus-shallow difference was 21.29 percentage points, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 11.15 to 36.63. The interval included zero at 100 km, with M6 neighbors and without isolation. Only 28 deep post-event counts support the main result. The test describes catalog pair timing. It does not establish a physical decay rate, recovery time or caused aftershocks. Ambient activity, region, selection, sparse counts, detection and catalog revision limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an external retrieval recipe, an independent count audit and a static figure are included.

display.caption: Deep minus shallow late count share for the main test and checks. Lines give pointwise conditional 95% three-year block intervals. The 100 km, M6 and no-isolation intervals include zero.
